notes: Gate for the editor load (perf/README.md). Numbers are per run of `npm run perf:editor`.

`baseline` is what the 2026-08-24 report measured *before* P2-004 was fixed, when every open tab kept a mounted viewer. It is here so a regression is read against the failure it came from, not against nothing.
`gate` is what the run must beat. Every limit is an upper bound except `inlineRowsTotalMin`, which is a floor. Raise one only together with the measurement that justifies it.

Latency is judged on `inputPaint` (keystroke → frame committed), not `inputFrame` (keystroke → rAF callback). A rAF callback runs before its frame's layout and paint, so gating on it would reward moving work past the callback — a win nobody could see. Both are still reported.

Memory is judged as deltas over an idle empty workbench, which the run samples before it opens anything. The old `rendererAfterCloseMiB <= 450` and `releasedAfterCloseMiB >= 80` were applied to workbench + load while being written as if they described the load. `releasedAfterCloseMiB` is still recorded, just no longer judged.

The run carries two loads and accounts for them separately: `loadDeltaMiB` is the peak while eight ~1 MB files are open as dirty tabs, `inlineDeltaMiB` the peak while the 内联 diff view is showing 350 changed regions per file. One combined peak would let either one's regression hide inside the other's headroom.

`openP95Ms` was split into `openFirstMs` and `openSteadyP95Ms`. Opening the first tab also fetches the lazily loaded editor chunk and every later one does not, so a single p95 over eight samples *is* the first sample — a one-time cost read as a per-tab regression, which is the confusion that nearly reverted the code split (docs/perf-gate-2026-08-28.md §9 #4). Split, each line means one thing and either can fail on its own.

`inlineRowsTotalMin` is the only lower bound here. `inlineRowsMountedMax` is the windowing invariant — what the inline diff view keeps in the DOM against what it models — and gating that alone would pass a fixture that happened to produce almost no rows. The floor is what stops the invariant passing vacuously, the same way `jsHeapRetainedMiB` fails rather than skips when the page cannot answer.

MEASURED over seven runs, 2026-08-30, win32 10.0.26100 / 32 cores / Electron 43.4.0 / Chrome 150, with the CodeMirror surface and the windowed inline view. (The first predates the dirty-buffer fix in docs/perf-gate-2026-08-28.md §10.4, which changes no allocation of consequence and is not an outlier on any line. The sixth is the first with the expandable ninth file, and every one of its numbers landed inside the ranges the earlier five had established — the extra file did not move the load.) Ranges below are min–max across those seven; every limit sits above the maximum, with headroom proportional to the spread that was actually observed rather than to a guess.

precise, spread under 10% — inline rows modelled 3150 (identical every run) · inline rows in the DOM 152 (identical every run) · inline expanded rows 3721, also 152 in the DOM · input→painted P95 12.3–12.7 ms · JS heap retained 7.0–7.2 MiB · inline scroll P95 10.2–12.5 ms · inline→painted 16.5–23.8 ms
moderate — open first 53.3–76.6 ms · open steady P95 33.3–52.3 ms · tab switch P95 24.4–54.1 ms · loadDelta 83.1–112.8 MiB
coarse, spread 31–150% — renderer peak 206.1–300.3 MiB · inlineDelta 108.3–202.1 MiB · jsHeapCommittedPeak 77.2–130.3 MiB · retainedDelta 41.8–106.1 MiB

The seventh run is why the headroom is sized to the spread rather than trimmed to the observed maximum: on unchanged code it set new maxima on four lines at once (open steady P95 42.0→52.3, renderer peak 280.8→300.3, inlineDelta 185.5→202.1, retainedDelta 100.5→106.1) and passed all of them. Limits trimmed to the previous maxima would have failed four checks and called it a regression.

`inlineFullRows*` gate the expanded branch of the inline view, which needs the ninth fixture file: 「显示全文」 is disabled past FULL_VIEW_LIMIT (4,000 lines) and the eight big ones are 12,001, so the branch was unreachable and the gate had only ever measured the collapsed one. It is the branch worth watching — collapsed, the row count follows the changes; expanded, it follows the file. One run so far: 1,079 rows collapsed → 3,721 expanded, with 152 in the DOM either way (24.5×), and 20.1 ms to expand.

Those last four are all downstream of one thing: how much V8 happened to have committed when a phase ended. Two runs recorded the *same* phase (「切完标签」) at 22.5/59.7 and 85.9/101.8 MiB used/committed. So they are coarse guards against a large allocation regression, not fine ones — the previous `jsHeapCommittedPeakMiB <= 100` was inside that noise and failed three times out of five on unchanged code, which is a broken gate, not a finding. What stays tight is the number that can actually detect a leak: `jsHeapRetainedMiB`, measured after a forced collection, sat at 7.0–7.1 MiB against a limit of 12 and did not move across any of the five runs.

`retainedDeltaMiB` was 110 and is now 140, and it is the same story as above rather than a concession: retention measured on the working set is mostly committed-but-free V8 pages, which V8 does not hand back promptly. Run 2 ended with 50.2 MiB committed and retained 41.8; run 4 ended with 77.2 committed and retained 95.6. The application is not holding it, and `jsHeapRetainedMiB` says so.

`jsHeapCommittedPeakMiB` still earns its place at 160: it gates the *cause* rather than the symptom, and the behaviour it was written against — serialising the whole ~948 KB document into React state on every keystroke and every tab switch — drove it far past this on a load without the inline phase at all. It will not catch a 20% regression. Nothing here will; that is what the measured spread says.
Re-derive these if the machine, the Electron version or the fixture changes. The ranges above are what makes that possible.

baseline.configuration: A DIFFERENT CONFIGURATION from this harness. Those numbers came from the user's real environment — 8 workspace roots, a real OMP agent, a real session — while the gate runs a fresh data directory, one root, the updater pointed at a dead proxy and no agent process. Only the shape of the regression is comparable; the absolute MiB are not. Reading this block as if it described the gate's own starting point is what once produced the claim that `released after close >= 80 MiB` was unsatisfiable by construction. It is not: the gate measures its own empty workbench every run (`rendererBaselineMiB`, ~96 MiB of renderer), and against that the eight tabs added ~400 MiB before the text surface was virtualised.
